The common misreading is that Maine claimed status had been wholly replaced by contract, leaving no fixed or inherited positions in modern law. He meant that the dominant basis of legal rights and duties shifted from ascribed position in the family group to voluntary agreements between individuals presumed free and equal, as an observed tendency that left status-like ties such as family relations intact. The team note is right that Maine's usage was loose, but his "status" centred on personal conditions fixed by family membership, not on wealth or taste.

CONFIDENCE: 80
